approach: Three changes meet in the throughput review. (1) athena-data: a `WasteFigures` struct (attempts per landing, wasted USD, first-attempt share), an optional defaulted `waste` field on `ThroughputReview`, and a `Wasted` trigger, so old records still parse. (2) status.rs: `waste_windows(records, window)` returns the newest window (partial allowed, with its landing count) and up to three full windows before it. `Throughput::compute` keeps the newest window, the one before it, the median for both, and a noise estimate per measure. `Throughput::text()` prints the three measures, so `athena status` shows them. (3) hestia.rs: `throughput_due` fires `Wasted` on a rise of more than 20% against the figures stored on the previous review. `throughput_review` never skips for an open design request: it names the request in the record's note and in THROUGHPUT.md, and it always asks the model on a due review. A pure `request_gate` decides only whether a design request is queued. Judged case: it queues only when a measure got worse by more than the noise, comparing the newest full 20-landing window with the 20 before it. The noise is the largest adjacent difference among the older full windows, and the note says how many differences were used (1 or 2). Not-judged case (fewer than 60 landings): it queues nothing, except for the very first review when no throughput design request is open. The note says 'not enough history: N of 60 landings'. The 25% slowdown rule and the stage-growth comparison are unchanged. No parser, stem list or reading rule changes, so refusal_corpus is not touched.

decisions.choice: Definitions. Landing = a landed request job. Attempt in a window = its landings + its did-not-land attempts. A did-not-land attempt is a request job with invocations that failed, was closed unlanded, or was stopped, using the same predicate as `unlanded_jobs` (status.rs:1015-1018), moved into a shared helper `did_not_land(job)`. Jobs still open count in neither side until they close. First-attempt landing = a landed job whose request is not 'try again on <job>' pointing at an earlier job that did work (`reading::retried_job`, reading.rs:1522). Wasted spend = `JobRecords::spent_usd` (store.rs:169) summed over the did-not-land attempts of the window.
decisions.reason: All figures come from job and invocation records, so no new record type is needed. Leaving open jobs out (finding 4) means attempts per landing is not inflated by work in flight, and every counted attempt has a close time to place it in a window. The retry link is the codebase's existing meaning of 'another attempt at the same change'.

rejected.option: Count every request job with invocations as an attempt
rejected.why: A running or waiting job is neither a landing nor wasted, which inflates attempts per landing and gives it no window.
Jobs stopped before an outcome carry no totals.

rejected.option: Count invocations or producer runs as attempts
rejected.why: A job's planner, critic and verifier runs are not attempts to land a change; the request's '58% of attempts did not land' is about jobs.

decisions.choice: Windows. Landed request jobs are ranked by (landing end, id), the ranking `landed_jobs_among_first` uses (status.rs:963), shared as a helper. Window 0 = the newest 20 landings, or all landings when there are fewer, plus every did-not-land attempt that closed at or after the oldest of those landings' end. Windows 1-3 = landings 21-40, 41-60, 61-80 plus did-not-land attempts closed between their cut times. A did-not-land attempt is placed by its closing outcome time, or its last invocation end if it has none. Window 0 is reported even when partial, with its landing count printed, as the median section does (status.rs:1003 uses saturating_sub). Windows 1-3 are reported only when full. `waste_windows(records, window)` takes the size so tests can use small windows; production passes THROUGHPUT_WINDOW. The median windows use the same cut over the measured landed jobs of `landed_jobs`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3: `athena status` and the first review show the three measures with fewer than 20 landings (the one-landing snapshot fixture shows 1.00, 0.00 USD, 100%). A thin window can never be the 'previous' window, so it cannot gate anything. The cut by landing end avoids a second time axis.

rejected.why: Hides the measures in any repository with under 20 landings and breaks the criterion 5 fixture, which has one landing.
Landings per day vary, so a window would not be 20 changes.

rejected.option: Waste figures over the measured jobs of landed_jobs() only
rejected.why: It drops landed jobs that ran no model, which are still landings.

decisions.choice: Trigger (`throughput_due(landed, median, waste: Option<WasteFigures>, latest)`) compares the newest-window figures with the figures stored on the previous review (new `waste: Option<WasteFigures>`), as the median trigger uses `window_median_minutes`, and needs a landing since that review. Rises: attempts per landing > previous x WORSEN_RATIO; wasted USD > previous x WORSEN_RATIO; first-attempt share < previous x (2 - WORSEN_RATIO). Floor for a rise from zero: when the previous wasted USD is 0, the spend rise counts only if attempts per landing also exceeds previous x WORSEN_RATIO. A previous review with no stored figures gives no waste trigger. Cadence still fires first at 10 landings beyond the previous review.
decisions.reason: A level that stays high triggers once, not on every landing, and old records stay valid. The zero floor ties a rise from zero to a measured ratio, not to a fixed cent value.

rejected.option: Trigger on newest 20 vs the 20 before, recomputed
rejected.why: A level that stays high would fire on every new landing.

rejected.option: Any wasted spend of 0.01 USD or more after a zero baseline
rejected.why: One failed run after a clean window would fire a review.
One `Wasted` variant suffices; the note names the measures that rose.

decisions.choice: The request gate. `request_gate` is pure and decides only whether a design request is queued; the model is asked on every due review. For each of four measures (median minutes, attempts per landing, wasted USD, first-attempt share) it forms, when windows 0, 1 and 2 are full (60 landings), the change = window 0 minus window 1 in the bad direction (median, attempts, spend up; share down), and the noise = the largest adjacent difference among the older full windows, |w1-w2| and |w2-w3| when window 3 is full, in that measure's own unit. A measure counts as beyond noise when change > noise (equal is within noise). A measure whose own windows are not full (for example fewer than 60 measured landed jobs for the median) is left out and the note says so. Judged: queue iff at least one measure is beyond noise; the note names each such measure with its change, noise and the number of differences used (1 or 2), or says 'within noise' or 'no measure worsened'. Not judged (no measure can be judged, under 60 landings): queue nothing and write 'not enough history: N of 60 landings, no request queued', with one exception: the first review (no earlier review) queues when no throughput design request is open, as today. The note and docs/design/hestia.md state this basis.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 1, 2, 6 and 7. The gate cannot queue on every review of a young repository, because 'cannot judge' now means 'do not queue', and it asks the model so a due review never does nothing. Change and noise are both differences between non-overlapping 20-landing windows, so they are like for like. The newest pair is excluded from its own noise. The stored-baseline comparison remains only the trigger's.

rejected.why: With the skip removed it queues a design request on every due review below 40 landings, even when nothing changed (finding 2).

rejected.option: Skip the model whenever the gate rejects
rejected.why: Most cadence reviews would do nothing, the complaint behind the request; the request limits queuing, not asking (finding 6).

rejected.option: Change = current vs the previous review's stored figures
rejected.why: That review may be 1 to 9 landings old, so its window overlaps window 0 and the change is diluted against a non-overlapping noise.
It is the 20% trigger again and does not adapt to the repository.

rejected.option: Standard error inside the two windows
rejected.why: Not 'noise between recent windows' as accepted, and needs per-job series.

decisions.choice: An open earlier design request no longer stops the review. The record's note says 'throughput design request <id> is still open; this review ran anyway', THROUGHPUT.md names the open request (id and title) so the proposal differs from it, the model is asked, and the proposal is recorded. A design request is queued only if the gate says so. When a request is open and the gate says queue, a second one is queued; both are linked by their reviews' `proposal.request_job`. When the gate says no, the proposal is recorded with `request_job: None` (as in the existing 'could not be queued' path).
decisions.reason: This is 'does not skip a run' plus 'notes the open request' plus 'only queues beyond noise'. No code assumes at most one throughput design request: `improvement_of` (hestia.rs:409-443) returns a set and `Plan::build_improving` (plan.rs:832-839) treats it as a set.

rejected.option: Keep the skip and reword it
rejected.why: The request calls the skipped runs 'did nothing'.

rejected.option: Ask the model but never queue while a request is open
rejected.why: A change beyond noise would then go unanswered until the open request closes; the plan leaves this as open question 1.

decisions.choice: Existing hestia tests are rewritten exactly where the new behaviour changes their assertions. The model is now asked on every due review, and with a previous review and under 60 landings nothing is queued. Rewritten: (a) `a_review_queues_one_design_request_...` (4411), second review: assert `proposal` is Some with `request_job == None`, the note holds 'still open', `open_design_requests` stays 1, the model log has 2 entries. (b) `a_median_rise_from_25_to_60_...` (4628): first half asserts proposal Some with `request_job None`, model log 1, one open design request and the unchanged slowdown assertions; second half asserts the model log is 2 and open design requests stay 1. (c) `unmeasured_landed_jobs_before_...` (4724): model log has 1 entry (was empty). (d) `a_flat_median_queues_nothing` (4757): model log has 1 entry, no request queued, nothing reported. (e) the 4790 rise-of-20-to-25-percent test, the improvement_of test (5116, whose second half queues no design request, so `items` stays empty) and the followup tests at 4526 and 4561 need no assertion change. `Lines` and `earlier_review` literal get the new field.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1: the dependents list now matches what decisions 4 and 5 do, test by test.

rejected.why: They assert the model is not called; under always-ask the log has more entries.

decisions.reason: Nothing to change there; a separate renderer would duplicate text() and could drift from what the review is given.

rejected.why: It would duplicate text() and could drift.

risks.risk: Every due review now calls the model, including those that queue nothing, so model spend per due review is no longer capped by an open request.
risks.mitigation: This matches today's cost when no request is open; reviews are due only on a 10-landing cadence or a rise; the record keeps the invocation; open question 3 asks the user.

risks.risk: Under 60 landings no request is queued after the first review, so a young repository gets fewer design requests than today.
risks.mitigation: The note says 'not enough history: N of 60 landings'; the model's proposal is still recorded; the CHANGELOG and hestia.md state the rule; open question 2 asks the user.

risks.risk: The noise rests on one difference with exactly 60 landings, so the gate can swing from run to run.
risks.mitigation: The note states the number of differences used (1 or 2) next to the noise.

risks.risk: Two design requests can be open at once and both get the guaranteed turn.
risks.mitigation: A second is queued only beyond noise; THROUGHPUT.md names the open request so the proposal differs; the criterion 4 test asserts `improvement_of` lists both; build_improving is set-based.

risks.risk: Failed-job fixtures end in the wrong window, so the criterion 1, 2(b) and 4(b) figures are off.
risks.mitigation: Failed jobs start 30 minutes after their slot's landing start and end after that landing's end (landings 20 min long, 2 h apart, hestia.rs:4281-4283); each test asserts `waste_windows` counts per window (40 attempts in criterion 1) before asserting results.

risks.risk: Window and retry reconstruction can drift: a landing record written later moves a landing end, and a 'try again on' link can point at a missing job.
risks.mitigation: A missing or unrun predecessor counts as no predecessor; the docs call the figures a reconstruction, as `previous_stage_medians` does.

risks.risk: A new record field makes a newer record unreadable by an older Athena because of deny_unknown_fields.
risks.mitigation: skip_serializing_if keeps the field out until the new code writes it; forward reading by old binaries is already limited for every new field in the crate.

risks.risk: Existing hestia tests fail if one of the rewrites in decision 6 is missed.
risks.mitigation: Step 6 lists each test and what it asserts afterwards; `cargo test --locked` runs them all.

demonstrations.method: A new status.rs test builds in-memory records with the existing helpers `timed_job` (status.rs:3261) and `loaded` (3343). It makes 20 landed jobs (index i starts at hour 2i on one day, 20 minutes long) and 20 failed jobs (`OutcomeState::Failed`). Failed job k starts 30 minutes after landing k starts, so each ends after the oldest landing's end (fixture timing for finding 5). Each failed job's invocation cost is set to 0.50 USD with `invocation(&job, 1, Role::Producer, 0.5)` (status.rs:2443). Landings 1-10 get request text 'try again on <id of failed job k-1>' in the form `reading::retry_reference` accepts, so 10 landings are retries. Failed jobs 10-19 are never retried. The test first asserts the window counts (20 landings, 20 unlanded, 40 attempts), then calls `waste_windows(&records, THROUGHPUT_WINDOW)` and `Throughput::compute(&records)`. A second case with only 20 landed jobs, and a third with 7 landed jobs (a partial window).
demonstrations.observes: Window 0 holds 40 attempts; attempts per landing is exactly 2.0; first-attempt share is exactly 0.5; wasted spend is 10.00 USD; `Throughput::compute(..).waste` shows the same figures. The no-failure case gives 1.0, 1.0, 0.0. The 7-landing case reports window 0 with landings == 7 and no previous window.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `waste_windows` the test does not compile. With attempts counted as landings only, attempts per landing is 1.0, and with no retry link the share is 1.0, so the 2.0 and 0.5 assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `status::waste_windows` (added by step 2) and `Throughput::compute`. Fixtures `timed_job`, `loaded`, `invocation` exist (status.rs:3261, 3343, 2443); the test edits request text and invocation cost on the loaded records. No double stands in front of the logic under test.

demonstrations.method: Two tests. (a) Pure `throughput_due(landed, median, waste, latest)` with `earlier_review_with_waste(10, 10.0, Some(attempts 1.5, wasted 2.00, share 0.8))`. Case A: 15 landed, same median 10.0, wasted 2.50, other figures equal returns Some(Wasted). Case C: all figures equal returns None. Case B: wasted 2.50 with no landing since (10 landed) returns None, and exactly 2.40 (20%) with 15 landed returns None. Case D: attempts 1.9, then share 0.6, each return Some(Wasted). Case E: previous with `waste: None` returns None. Case F: previous wasted 0.0 and current 0.5 with attempts equal returns None; with attempts up 25% returns Some(Wasted). (b) Review level: 80 landings in four windows (`seed_landed(.., 0, 80, 10.0)`, median flat), failed attempts from `seed_failed` at 1.00 USD each: windows 3, 2, 1, 0 hold 2, 5, 2, 10. The previous review (75 landings, median 10.0, stored wasted 2.00) is stored with `put_earlier_review_with_waste`. `athena.throughput_review(&Quiet)` runs with `throughput_model(6.0)` injected through `athena_with`.
demonstrations.observes: (a) The Some/None results above, with the median identical in A and C. (b) The record has trigger `Wasted` and `window_median_minutes` 10.0, and the model log has one entry. Spend rose 10 vs 2 (change 8) against noise 3, so the gate queues one design request and the note names wasted spend as beyond noise.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the waste argument and the Wasted branch, Case A returns None because the median is unchanged, and the review-level case returns Ok(None) because nothing is due.

Existing fixtures: `athena_with`, `seed_landed`, `put_earlier_review`, `throughput_model` (hestia.rs:4233-4346), `earlier_review` literal (4348). Step 6 adds `earlier_review_with_waste`, `put_earlier_review_with_waste` and `seed_failed(dir, athena, slot, usd)`: a Failed job built with `timed_job` starting 30 minutes after slot's landing start, producer cost set via `invocation(..).cost`, committed with `put`. demonstrations.method: Three tests. (a) Pure `request_gate`: change 0.1 attempts against noise 0.3 gives queue false and a note containing 'within noise'; change 0.5 against 0.3 gives queue true, naming the measure, change, noise and 'differences'; change exactly equal to the noise is within noise; a share that fell counts as worse; a measure that improved or did not move gives 'no measure worsened'; under 60 landings gives queue false with 'not enough history: N of 60'; the same with no earlier review and no open request gives queue true, and with an open request gives false. (b) Review level, the criterion 2(b) fixture (80 landings, flat median, 1.00 USD failed attempts, windows 3/2/1 hold 2/5/2, so spend noise 3 USD, attempts noise 0.15, share and median noise 0) with the previous review citing the open d000. Within case: window 0 holds 4 failed (spend +2, attempts +0.1); the stored baseline 2.00 makes `Wasted` fire. Beyond case: window 0 holds 10 failed (spend +8, attempts +0.4). Both cases use `throughput_model(6.0)`. (c) Beyond case also asserts two design requests are open and `improvement_of` lists both.
demonstrations.observes: Within: the record has trigger Wasted, the model log has one entry, the proposal has `request_job None`, no design request is queued (still only d000), and the note contains 'within noise', 'still open' and the count of differences (2). The pure cases give the results above.

open_questions: User: When an earlier design request is still open and the change is beyond noise, should a second design request be queued (this plan does, and tells the model about the open one), or should the review record the proposal and queue nothing until the open request closes?
User: Below 60 landings the noise cannot be estimated. This plan queues nothing then, except for the very first review, and says so in the note. Should it instead queue on any worsening, or wait?

User: This plan asks the model on every due review, as it does today when no request is open, so a due review costs one model call even when no request is queued. Should a review whose change is within noise skip the model to save that cost?
